document.title: Afghanistan: Taliban Seeks Low Profile Relations With the USG – At Least For Now (Islama 08520)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban Biography: The Structure and Leadership of the Taliban 1996-2002
document.note: [Secret] Abdul Jalil, self-described number two for the Taliban on foreign affairs, delivers a friendly message from Mullah Omar. The Taliban want good relations with the U.S. but unpublicized contacts, to avoid accusations of being an anti-Shia tool of the U.S. Jalil is said to make a good impression and to work for Mullah Ghaus.

HAD LEARNED HIS ENGLISH IN AN ICRC HOSPITAL IN PESHAWAR IN 1981, WHEN HE WAS RECEIVING TREATMENT FROM A LEG WOUND SUFFERED IN THE JIHAD
A PERSONAL MESSAGE FROM TALIBAN LEADER MAULVI OMAR

events.description: Abdul Jalil met US DCM at DCM residence in Islamabad and delivered Mullah Omar's message seeking low-key relations.
Jalil treated for leg wound at ICRC hospital in Peshawar, learned English.
Abdul Jalil met the DCM at his residence and delivered a message from Maulvi Omar seeking low-profile relations with the U.S.
U.S. Embassy Islamabad cable reporting the Jalil meeting.
Jalil treated for a leg wound at an ICRC hospital in Peshawar, where he learned English.
Masood reportedly accepted Russian support during the jihad.

key_claims: Mullah Omar sent a message via Jalil seeking quiet, low-key contacts with the US.
Taliban fear accusations from Iran, Hekmatyar, Rabbani and Masood that they are a US tool, resonating among Hazaras.
Taliban want to establish relations first with Saudi Arabia and the UAE before publicly opening relations with the US.
Taliban claim no problem with Dostam or Tajiks but regard Masood as the problem.
Jalil clarified Taliban foreign affairs hierarchy: Ghaus first, Jalil deputy, Stanakzai deputy for reconstruction.
